claim: Compagnie Corsaire runs the Saint-Malo to Dinard sea bus from 28 March to 3 July 2026; crossing takes 10 minutes; one-way adult €6.30 (rate A) and return €8.90; child one-way €4.50.
quote: Seabus Saint-Malo Dinard 28 march to 3rd july 2026 ... In the space of 10 minutes, you will be in Dinard or Saint-Malo. Adult return: €8.90 | One-way: €6.30. Child return: €6.30 | One-way: €4.50.

claim: Official 2026 sea bus spring timetable is published as a downloadable PDF on the Compagnie Corsaire schedules page.
quote: please find below our timetable Saint-Malo/Dinard from 28th march to 3rd july

claim: The Promenade du Clair de Lune hugs the Rance estuary with sea-spray-wet sections and panoramic views to Saint-Malo's ramparts; visitors describe a 15-minute walk to the casino.
quote: You are virtually on top of the sea which u can see/hear crashing up against the rocks ... On the other side of the Rance, you can see the ramparts of Saint Malo ... It takes about 15 minutes to walk and you'll arrive at the casino

claim: The Alfred Hitchcock bronze stands on the embankment of Plage de l'Écluse next to the casino, with birds on his shoulder referencing The Birds, commemorating Dinard's British Film Festival.
quote: On the embankment of Plage de l'Ecluse, next to the Casino you walk almost past the bronze monument ... Pictured here with birds on his shoulder. The Birds!

claim: Plage de l'Écluse is a broad southwest-facing crescent of golden sand with blue-and-white striped tents fixed since the 1890s, a seawater pool, and Dinard is dubbed 'Cannes of the North'.
quote: the famous blue-and-white striped tents that line the promenade ... have been a fixture since the 1890s ... sometimes dubbed the 'Cannes of the North'

claim: Dinard's 'Cannes of the North' reputation grew from late-19th-century American and British aristocrats building villas on the cliff tops; it remains 'one of the most British' French coastal resorts and hosts the Dinard British Film Festival (founded 1989).
quote: Dinard's reputation as the 'Cannes of the North' has attracted a wide variety of stars ... In the late 19th century, American and British aristocrats made Dinard a fashionable summer resort and built stunning villas on the cliff tops

claim: Dinard preserves nearly 400 protected Belle Époque villas accessible via the tourist office's walking tours, with Villa les Roches Brunes classified as a Historical Monument.
quote: nearly 400 protected villas to discover by following our walking tours ... Villa les Roches Brunes ... Classified as a Historical Monument

claim: Villa Eugénie (the former Musée du Site Balnéaire) is being converted into inclusive housing by the Diadème association under a 40-year lease signed 27 November 2025, with work starting in 2026 — meaning the museum is not operating in 2026.
quote: Les travaux de réhabilitation débuteront en 2026 ... une ouverture prévisionnelle en avril 2027

claim: The City of Dinard confirms Villa Eugénie's rehabilitation will deliver six inclusive-housing units and a solidarity restaurant, with provisional reopening April 2027.
quote: Les travaux débuteront prochainement pour une ouverture prévisionnelle en avril 2027.

claim: Saint-Lunaire and Saint-Briac-sur-Mer, west of Dinard, are quieter family seaside resorts with turquoise waters, fine sandy beaches, and Belle Époque villas — Saint-Lunaire's centre shaped by Haitian businessman Sylla Laraque.
quote: Saint-Lunaire's town center bears the radiance of the Belle Époque and reflects the passion of Sylla Laraque, a wealthy Haitian businessman who made Saint-Lunaire one of the first seaside resorts on the Emerald Coast

claim: Sea water at Plage de l'Écluse in May–June ranges roughly 12–18°C; a wetsuit is recommended for comfortable swimming.
quote: The sea at Plage de l'Écluse - Dinard feels cool so don't forget to pack your wetsuit

claim: Cap Fréhel sits roughly 45 km / ~52 minutes by road from Saint-Malo, putting it (and adjacent Fort la Latte) outside a strict 30-km radius from Saint-Méloir-des-Ondes.

The Promenade du Clair de Lune is lined with palm trees, mimosas and agapanthus giving it an 'almost Mediterranean feel', and Dinard has hosted a British/Irish cinema festival every autumn since 1990.
quote: Palm trees, mimosas, and agapanthus line this pedestrian path, giving it an almost Mediterranean feel ... Since 1990, Dinard has hosted an annual fall festival dedicated to British and Irish cinema.
